For a metal–ligand complex  
CaY²⁻ ⇌ Ca²⁺ + Y⁴⁻

the formation (stability) constant is  

Kf = [CaY²⁻] / ( [Ca²⁺][Y⁴⁻] ) = 5 × 10¹⁰.

Let the stoichiometric concentration of the complex be C = 0.020 M.  
Let x = [Ca²⁺] released by the slight dissociation of the complex.

At equilibrium  
[Ca²⁺] = x  
[Y⁴⁻]  = x  
[CaY²⁻] = C – x ≈ 0.020 M (because the complex is very stable, x ≪ C)

Insert these into Kf:

Kf = (C – x)/(x²) ≈ C / x²

x² = C / Kf  
x² = 0.020 M / (5 × 10¹⁰)  
x² = 4 × 10⁻¹³  

x = √(4 × 10⁻¹³)  
x ≈ 6.3 × 10⁻⁷ M

Thus the concentration of free Ca²⁺ ions is about 6.3 × 10⁻⁷ M.

Answer: D
